Subject: Planned WestUS2 maintenance: kernel ABI update + rolling reboots (Jul 11)

Hi Leslie / Acme team,

I wanted to give advance notice of a planned maintenance window in our WestUS2 region that may affect inference sessions for your workloads. Our infra team will perform a kernel ABI update followed by coordinated rolling reboots of GPU hosts to ensure driver compatibility and stability for the next runtime release.

Planned window:
- Start: Sun, Jul 11, 2026 00:00 PDT
- End: Sun, Jul 11, 2026 06:00 PDT
- Expected per-node disruption: 15-45 seconds while processes drain and restart; most requests will be transparently retried.

What we're changing:
- Kernel ABI bump to align with updated NVIDIA driver stack
- Targeted host reboots (rolling across AZs) with staged health checks and KV-cache warmup

Mitigation and customer impact:
- We will perform rolling restarts to avoid region-wide downtime; at no point will more than ~12% of capacity be offline.
- Short-lived connection resets may occur; clients using retry/backoff should see negligible impact.
- If you have pinned model versions or long-running KV-cached streams, we recommend scheduling critical batches outside the window or using replica in another region (e.g., WestUS3) during the window.

Attachments: maintenance playbook + canary checklist are attached.
[Attachment: westus2-maintenance_playbook.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: canary-checklist.txt (text)]

If you have blackout constraints (legal filing, demo, major deadline) within this window, please let me know by end of week and we'll coordinate an exemption or alternate scheduling. Otherwise we will proceed with the published date.

Thanks — I will post updates to status.redwood.ai and send a reminder 24 hours before the start.

Best,
Monica Patel

Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned WestUS2 maintenance: kernel ABI update + rolling reboots (Jul 11)

Hi Leslie — quick answers inline and next steps.

1) KV-cache: we expect short-lived KV-cache warm/depopulate on the affected hosts. Sticky pinned sessions may experience a short rewarm delay (~20-60s) as requests are routed to warmed hosts. Recommendation: use our client retry with exponential backoff (start 100ms, cap 3s, max 5 retries) and enable request hedging for critical calls.

2) SLA credits: planned maintenance is excluded from SLA credit triggers if published with 72+ hours notice. That said, if we have unexpected degradation beyond our projections (for example, >10% sustained error rate for >30min after the window), we will classify that as an incident and handle credit requests per the SLA process.

Operational plan:
- Jul 11 00:00 PDT: begin canary (3 hosts) — 60m observation
- If canary is healthy, proceed to rolling batches by AZ with automated health gates
- Ops on-call: Marcus Lin; Backup ops: Evelyn Hart; Eng escalation: Aditya Rao

I've scheduled a 30-minute sync with the ops crew on Jul 10 to confirm runbook readiness and cutover steps. I'll post the runbook link and the status page as we approach the date.

Monica
